scenario: AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

message.reasoning:
The scenario describes a husband who prioritizes watching video game streams (with cash giveaways) over spending time with his wife and family, despite her requests. He also has a history of excessive spending on in-app purchases for the game, which the wife has concerns about. The wife feels disappointed and upset.

Key points:
- The husband agreed to build the kids' bikes (a chore) while watching streams, but then left for an errand and returned to continue watching.
- When asked to turn off the stream to spend time together, he refused, stating it's not okay to expect him to stop doing what he enjoys just because she wants him to do something she enjoys.
- The wife notes that he would likely stop if she allowed him to spend money on the game, but she is hesitant due to past overspending.
- The husband's behavior seems to disregard the wife's feelings and the importance of shared time, especially in the evening when family time is typical.
- The husband's refusal to engage in family time and his prioritization of personal entertainment, especially when it conflicts with agreed-upon responsibilities and marital expectations, appears selfish and dismissive.

Morally, in a committed relationship, partners should consider each other's needs and make reasonable efforts to spend quality time together. While individuals are entitled to personal leisure, consistently prioritizing personal entertainment over a partner's request for shared time, especially without compromise, can be seen as a failure to uphold relational responsibilities. The husband's stance that he should not have to stop his enjoyable activity for something his wife enjoys is particularly problematic, as relationships require mutual accommodation.

Additionally, the financial aspect (in-app purchases) adds another layer of irresponsibility, but the core issue is the disregard for the wife's request for connection.

Thus, the husband's action (refusing to turn off the stream to spend time with his wife) is morally unacceptable because it shows a lack of consideration for his partner's feelings and the relationship's needs.
